ours-embed.short: Night School's skip-gram, trained for this film
ours-embed.citation: media/school/embeddings/facts.json, written by tools/school/fill_embeddings.mjs from system/school/embeddings.mjs: skip-gram with negative sampling (32 numbers per word, window 1 to 2, 5 noise words, 5 epochs, seed 1) on the guides' corpus; a finite-difference check of the hand-written gradient (worst 5.3e-7).
claims: Same-kind nearest neighbour share: 26% at the start (shuffle control mean 22%, 95% interval 9% to 39%); highest of the 12 snapshots at 5% of training (72%), 65% at the end, from one seed; held-out loss falls at every snapshot (2.14 at 5%, 1.92 at the end).
Seed 1 against each of four other seeds: 75% to 80% of each word's three nearest neighbours agree (pairs among seeds 2 to 5 not measured).
ours-embed.n: 46 entries (44 words and two marks); 5 seeds.
ours-embed.interval: Range over seeds, stated; shuffle control 95% interval in facts.json.

mikolov2013.short: Mikolov and others 2013, Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality
mikolov2013.citation: Mikolov, T., Sutskever, I., Chen, K., Corrado, G., Dean, J. (2013). Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality. NeurIPS 26. arXiv:1310.4546.
mikolov2013.read: full text of arXiv 1310.4546v1, sections 2 and 2.2 (equation 4, the noise distribution, k from 5 to 20 for small data); the skip-gram architecture itself is from arXiv 1301.3781, section 3.2
claims: The skip-gram model learns an input and an output vector for every word, trained so a word's vector predicts the words around it (section 2).

Negative sampling replaces the full softmax: each real (word, context) pair is pushed together and k words drawn from a noise distribution (the unigram distribution to the 3/4 power) are pushed apart (section 2.2, equation 4).
mikolov2013.does_not_prove: That the learned neighbours reflect meaning beyond how words are used in the training text.

ours-model.short: Night School's tiny transformer, its word table
claims: The attention model's word table puts 80% of words next to a same-kind word; its top-3 neighbour lists overlap the skip-gram's by 33% (chance about 7%; shuffled control 2% to 12%).
ours-model.does_not_prove: Which table is better; they were trained for different games.
